name: Oberlaa
desc: Very Viennese cafes, really delicious bakery and well known confectionery. Also some choice of soups and mains. Several locations, mostly in Innere Stadt.

name: Aida
desc: Chic but artificial design, mediocre quality, depends on location and luck. Many cafés across Vienna and Lower Austria. Their menus have a very useful graphical design indicating the precise ingredients and proportions i

name: Wein & Co
desc: A chain shop for wine lovers featuring a wine bar in every location. Shop locations include Naschmarkt, Mariahilfer Straße, near Burggarten and near Stephansplatz.

name: Why Not
desc: Vienna's mainstream everyday gay disco. The crowd is varied. It is in the 1st District at Tiefer Graben 22 (Herrengasse U3). Saturdays are house music free.

name: Rosa Lilla Villa
desc: A gay resource center with an excellent bar and restaurant. (Pilgramgasse U4)

name: Esterházykeller
desc: Atmospheric old (since 1683) cellar restaurant serving good, cheap, wine, beer, and simple traditional food. Prices budget to moderate. A good place to go if you just want a drink and some grub, but still want to enjoy s

name: Schachtelwirt
desc: Good schnitzel, potatoes and pork. The food is very good, different from what you can eat in typical Austrian restaurants. Cool atmosphere.

name: Chattanooga
desc: Fast food versions of local food. Not bad if you are on a budget and do not have much time to spare.

name: Gasthaus zum Holunderstrauch
desc: Recommendation if you are looking for home-style, local food. The atmosphere is cozy. The service provides competent and friendly advice.

name: Maschu Maschu
desc: Good for veggies and meat eaters alike. Maschu Maschu is an Israeli fast food joint that serves some of the best falafel in the world. A healthy and gut-busting falafel and beer should leave you set up for the day (they

name: Trzesniewski
desc: The snack bar sells small breads (Brötchen) with specific spread (Aufstrich). One has many choices including vegetarian. The place is very full at lunch time, but the queue advances quickly. They only use organic eggs. T

name: Fladerei Salzgries
desc: Really nice flat bread. Open until late. Plenty of choice for vegetarians too.

name: Leberkas-Pepi
desc: Authentic local fast food. Very good meatloaf and other convenient Vienna traditional light meals.

name: Würstelstand zum Hohen Markt
desc: Legendary stall at Hoher Markt. As always great sausages.

name: Wiener Würstl
desc: Great sausage. The seller can explain everything about all types of sausages.

name: Würstelstand am Schottentor
desc: A lovely spot for street meat. Good flavors and great/friendly service.

name: Palmenhaus
desc: Good value for money, great ambience with imperial decor. Large mains served with a bowl of salad included. Very high ceilings, full of air and palms. Friendly staff speaks fluent English. Children-safe wide couches. Con

name: Inigo
price: Mains around €10, average dinner with a
desc: Modern and diverse cuisine, not crowded but most visitors are local. Charming modern interior instead of imperial chic. Overall, a rare combination of features. Menu has equal parts for vegetarians and carnivores. Friend

name: Brezl-Gwölb
desc: A very nice restaurant with a cellar dating back to the 17th century. The furniture consists of parts from three centuries. A place that deserves the label gemütlich. They play classical music and serve some really uniqu

name: Figlmüller
desc: Famous for Wienerschnitzel. They claim to have the biggest schnitzel in the world. If you are not really hungry, one may easily be enough for two people (just ask for a second plate). Traditionally, you would want a pota

name: Le Bol
hours: M-F from 08:00, Sa Su and holidays from 10:00
desc: Fine French Provencal-style fare with a communal table at the center, goat cheese salad is highly recommended ({{EUR

name: Reinthaler Gasthaus
desc: One of the better traditional Beisl restaurants, with old fashioned food priced below comparable places. Daily specials usually include a couple of vegetarian options.

name: Zum Leupold
desc: A bourgeois Viennese restaurant offering good seasonal local food. In summertime you can sit outdoors.

name: Ristorante Rossini
desc: An Italian place serving good mostly authentic Italian food.

name: Vietthao
desc: The Vietnamese restaurant offers lots of vegetarian choices. Their vegetables are well prepared using good herbs combinations.

name: Akakiko
desc: Part of a local chain. Informal and popular place serving generic but reasonably priced Japanese and Korean dishes. The menu has a vegetarian section. Quick service by efficient waiters.

name: Artner am Franziskanerplatz
desc: Belongs to a famous winery Artner. It offers creative, fresh fare that tends to be on the lighter side than most Austrian cuisine. Excellent wine cellar, reservations recommended.

name: Bauer
desc: The restaurant since 25 years serves excellent food with Viennese charme and a big wine choice. It has one Michelin star.

name: Bristol Lounge
desc: The big lunch room in the Hotel Bristol reopened with the original art déco chandeliers and decorated ceiling. The restaurant may serve as elegant after Opera dinner.

name: Daihachi
desc: Sushi bar popular with business travellers. Serves fresh and tasty fish that comes at a high price.

name: Fabios
desc: Italian fish restaurant combined with bar/lounge for Vienna's glitterati. Quality is excellent.

name: Palais Coburg
desc: The gourmet restaurant is handled by 2 Michelin-starred chef Silvio Nickol. It offers a 5-, 7- or 9-course menu. The seasonal wine card is exquisite.

name: Plachutta
desc: A very nice restaurant that specialises in beef (claimed to be only local and from trusted farmers) and has some flavour of traditional Austrian cuisine. Try the Tafelspitz, it comes in a copper pan and still is in the s

name: Procacci
desc: Excellent northern Italian fare with a range of fine specialties. Slightly small portions but an extensive wine list to drown this particular sorrow in. Reservations recommended.

name: TIAN Restaurant
desc: Star chef Paul Ivić from Tyrol leads one of only two vegetarian Michelin-starred restaurants in Europe, with an excellent wine selection. Occasionally he also offers workshops. Reservations can be made [https://www.tian-

name: Unkai
desc: The Japanese cook Hiroshi Sakai once governed this place that serves authentic Japanese food. One dines on the top floor of a splendid Viennese palace, that is nowadays the Grand Hotel. It has an excellent choice of spec

name: Vestibül
desc: Viennese bourgeois restaurant cooked by Christian Domschitz.

name: Weinbotschaft
desc: The restaurant offers a menu with freshly cooked organic ingredients – from the classic Wiener Schnitzel to Chocolate-Almond-Cake without flour and Bio-Fruit-Ice-Cream.

name: Zimolo
desc: This hidden gem features Italian food. You can sit outside in the small pedestrian street.

name: Eissalon am Schwedenplatz
desc: Maybe the most popular place. You can choose from a lot of different flavors, but it's always crowded and you often have to stand in a queue for a few minutes.

name: Eissalon am Tuchlauben (Perizzolo)
desc: Another excellent and popular ice cream parlour. Ask for the Special Nougat ice cream.

name: Eis-Greissler
desc: A small ice parlour that has been overrun by customers since its opening in 2011. They sell excellent organic ice cream, made from milk of their own organic milk farm and without artificial flavours. It is worth the wait

name: Ferrari Gelato
desc: The Italian ice cream shop produces on the spot their own with exquisite ingredients like piemontese hazelnuts, caramelised pine nuts or fresh fruits.

name: Zanoni & Zanoni Gelateria
desc: In the same district as Eissalon. Popular with Viennese and tourists for its huge €2 cones to go.

name: Café Bräunerhof
desc: Thomas Bernhard used to come here daily as do many other Viennese literate. It exists since more than 35 years. Happily expect Viennese grumpy senior waiters.

name: Café Central
desc: One of the most famous Vienna coffee houses, which opened in 1876, has been authentically restored. Beautiful premises inside the Palais Ferstel, it is too touristy and a bit more expensive for having a meal, but can be

name: Café Diglas
desc: Famous traditional coffeehouse, and equally good place for having a meal. They opened a second branch on Fleischmarkt.

name: Café Frauenhuber
desc: This traditional café already existed at the times of Mozart and Beethoven. It serves Viennese food.

name: Café Gerstner
desc: A very traditional Viennese café, hence visitors take their time to enjoy the lovely cakes.

name: Café Hawelka
desc: One of the most famous intellectual cafes in Vienna. Established in 1939. Surprisingly cheap for its location and its fame and can get quite cozy. Josephine Hawelka (former owner, deceased 2005) was proud of the marriage

name: Café Landtmann
price: Breakfast sets €7-12.50, menu of the day
hours: 07:30-24:00; all menus until 11:30, except Franz L
desc: Old café, cozy and romantic. Used to be frequented by Sigmund Freud. Delicious food and desserts.

name: Café Museum
desc: This cafe was designed by famous architect Adolf Loos, however the interior has been entirely refitted (most recently from 2010). Serves food, coffee, teas, and other drinks. Casual, quiet atmosphere.

name: Café Prückel
hours: Daily 08:00-22:00; live music M W F 19:00-22:00; c
desc: Established in 1903. Quite the hang-out in the evening, during the day this cafe is a bit more laissez-faire.

name: Café Sacher Wien
desc: The Café Sacher, directly in front of the Opera House, of course serves the famous cake Sacher Torte.

name: Sacher Eck
desc: The Sacher bar next to their shop is on the Corner of Kärtner Strasse and is a bit less formal than the traditional café. Still on rush hours expect some waiting time to get seated in order to be able to order the "Sache

name: Cafe Schwarzenberg
desc: Beautiful traditional Viennese café with view on the Schwarzenbergplatz and the Ring avenue. It has fine pastries and coffee choices.

name: Café Tirolerhof
desc: Quaint, traditional café with art deco accents. Established in 1900.

name: Conditorei Sluka
desc: A very traditional small Viennese café, opened at the end of the 19th century by Josef and Josefine Sluka, serves excellent pastries and bread. To the breakfast you can order oeuf poché. The choice on the menu is adjuste

name: Demel
desc: Café and confectionary shop. Good pastries are ubiquitous in Vienna, but Demel is considered by many to have the best of all and indeed was once the pastry caterer to the Imperial household. As a result of this it is usu

name: Kleines Café
desc: As the name suggests, this café is rather small. It was created by architect Hermann Czech during the 1970s for notable Austrian actor Hanno Pöschl, who still owns it. It is a popular meeting place for artists and actors

name: Vollpension
desc: Intergenerational café run as a social business: the cakes are baked by senior citizens to their own family recipes and served in a vintage living-room setting. Vegetarian lunch menu on weekdays, shaded outdoor seating i

name: 1516 Brewing Company
desc: A brewery and a bar with quality beers. The food menu includes Viennese classics as well as standard American bar food like burgers, chicken wings, and BBQ ribs. 1516 particularly caters to American and British expats, a

name: Alt Wien
desc: This cafe/restaurant/bar is on a very medieval-looking lane in the central district and is a time warp of another kind: its folky-bohemian atmosphere could convince you that you're in North Beach or Greenwich Village, ci

name: Bonbonniere Tagesbar
desc: Special establishment where the time stood still.

name: Dino's
desc: The bar serves classical cocktails.

name: Flex
desc: You have not been to Vienna if you have not been to the Flex, particularly if you are younger than thirty. The meeting point of the off-mainstream, bohemian, artsy people. During the summer nights when it is warm, there

name: Loos American Bar
desc: Built in 1908, this small bar was designed by Adolf Loos and inspired by his stay in the US from 1893-1896, and will delight fans of Art Deco. Famous for its architecture and interior decoration, it is a time warp of Vie

name: Roberto
desc: The former chief bar keeper of the Loos Bar, Roberto Pavlovic opened a new American bar. It serves aperitifs 16:00–18:00, and 16:00–20:00 Champagne price is reduced. 200 cocktails to choose from.

name: Schrittesser
desc: The place is specialised on Carinthian drinks and food. Speck in all kinds is served. Carinthian noodles and Schnaps are recommended too. The bar is hidden behind the Viennese university.

name: Bermuda Triangle
desc: A night-life area popular for young people as the alcoholic beverages are cheap.

name: Club Passage
desc: An upscale club.

name: Volksgarten Clubdiskothek
desc: Up-market.

name: Badeschiff
desc: An orange boat. All sorts of [https://www.facebook.com/badeschiff.at/events? events and parties] go on here, and in summer you can take a dip in the outdoor [http://www.badeschiff.at/#baden pool-barge] during the day. Th

name: Paninoteca
desc: Small delicious little Italian sandwiches for takeaway. They offer free Wi-Fi.

name: Salon Wichtig
desc: Dubbed the best curry in town, it has vegetarian options and the food is freshly cooked. Most people choose takeaway; one can sit nearby in front of Karlskirche.

name: Aromat
desc: This place has an excellent different dinner menu with vegetarian option every week. It has the best crêpes in Vienna, but is unfortunately a smokers restaurant. Reservations are strongly recommended.

name: Babette's
desc: The small kitchen-bookstore serves an excellent lunch menu, with usually one vegetarian choice. The tables/bar can accommodate only a small number of people. Patrons can watch the food preparation and learn cooking tips.

name: Chang
desc: Next to the upscale restaurant there is the simpler one, which shares the same kitchen. Vegetarians will find good choices.

name: Gasthaus Ubl
desc: The Austrian restaurant "Wirtshaus" serves traditional Viennese in authentic decor.

name: Kojiro Sushi-Bar
desc: The first sushi bar in Vienna is a still-thriving crowded place. It is really small and easily missed. The green tea is free for customers.

name: Kojiro
desc: The newer second branch of Kojiro is on a little square, where one can sit outside. It has a daily Japanese lunch menu and excellent sushi.

name: Nagoya Sushi
desc: The Korean restaurant got modernised in 2013 and added Japanese food to its menu. It now sells fresh Sushi also for the go. They kept many Korean choices.

name: Tewa am Naschmarkt
desc: Very bio place, popular with the early thirty-something bohemian locals.

name: Artner auf der Wieden
desc: Belongs to a famous winery. Offers creative, fresh fare that tends to be on the lighter side than most Austrian cuisine. It has a 2 or 3-course business lunch menu offering, where one of the two options is vegetarian. Ex

name: Coté Sud
desc: This small bistro cooks French cuisine with consistent good quality.

name: Otto e Mezzo
desc: This restaurant, named after the Fellini film, is an Italian gem and offers a daily lunch menu. The Italian wines are well chosen and the pasta is lovely.

name: Schikaneder
desc: The bar next to the cinema is popular with the mixed alternative crowd. Seats are usually only available if you go early.

name: Roxy Club
desc: Operating since 1991 (with a short break only in 2012), this place stands out if you like stylish evenings with good music, including funk, soul, and hip hop. Look out for a small door to go downstairs.

name: Wieden Bräu
desc: The brewery serves typical Austrian food. The beers are Märzen, Hell, Dunkel, Gemischtes and a monthly one.

name: Cafe Amacord
desc: This café serves a lunch menu and international food choices including lots of vegetarian options. It has a nice laid back atmosphere, and is one of Vienna's rare non-smoking cafés. It has good Austrian whine and red win

name: Café Anzengruber
desc: This place is packed for football games and serves mostly beer and wine. The Schnitzel is highly recommended by locals.

name: Heuer am Karlsplatz
desc: This café is located very centrally on Karlsplatz, in the cube building of the Kunsthalle next to the University of Technology. It got relaunched in 2014 with stylish exterior and Thonet chairs inside. With good weather

name: Radlager
desc: The very stylish bike shop sells excellent coffee from an Italian espresso machine with Neapolitan roasted beans, juices, small sandwiches and salads.

name: Süssi
desc: A French tea salon that sells excellent French patisserie (Macarons). Its interior is extravagant.

name: The breakfastclub
desc: The place's specialty is good breakfasts, with many choices including vegetarian.

name: Café Wortner
desc: A traditional Viennese café with a nice interior, but beware of the smoke and don't expect too much for the food. Wi-Fi access.

name: Vollpension
desc: The original location of Vienna's intergenerational café, opened in 2015: senior citizens bake cakes to their own family recipes in a living-room-style interior. Breakfast served into the afternoon, outdoor seating, dogs

name: Bortolotti
addr: Mariahilfer Straße 22 and 94 (the latter closed during winter!)
desc: An ice cream parlour worth visiting. Ask particularly for the Campari-Orange ice cream or try some other exotic flavors.

name: Kolar Zieglergassemore
desc: Nice pubs/beisls. They have a tasty Fladenbrot as well as their own beer.

name: Maschu
desc: A trendy hang out place with its own unique vibe, in the area of the city frequented by art students. It is famous for its falafel.

name: Natsu II
desc: Serves decent sushi.

name: Schnitzelwirt Schmidt
desc: The traditional Viennese food is excellent and served in truly prodigious portions. The Bauernschmaus (Farmer's Feast), a nearly incapacitatingly large schnitzel plate, which in combination with any of the wonderful on-t

name: Amerlingbeisl
desc: The restaurant has a good selection of food with vegetarian options too. Inside smoking is permitted, but this is not so much of a problem for non-smokers in summer when it's possible to sit outside. The bar serves beer,

name: Bombay
desc: It serves the best Bombay Gin in Vienna. Among Indian restaurants in Vienna it is an institution, offering good food and large servings for reasonable prices.

name: DschungelCafe
desc: A very child-friendly cafe and restaurant, located in the same building as the DschungelWien.at children's theater.

name: Gasthaus Grünauer
desc: A Viennese restaurant serving high-quality food with a good selection of wines.

name: MQdaily
desc: Located next to the entry of the MQ, this place is quite small and packed.

name: I Ragazzi
desc: This Italian restaurant has good pizzas and pastas for good prices. Their fish soup is highly recommended. Outdoor seating is available in the summer.

name: I Terroni
desc: Same crew as I Ragazzi but less crowded. The restaurant serves good Italian pizzas and pastas.

name: Tian Bistro am Spittelberg
hours: Tu 17:00-23:00, W-F 11:00-23:00, Sa Su and holiday
desc: Operated by star chef Paul Ivić of TIAN Restaurant, the bistro serves more affordable meals than at his main restaurant, all of them vegetarian with many vegan options. Reservations can be made [http://www.tian-bistro.co

name: Le Troquet
desc: A popular French bistro in a shabby chic setting. They play jazz and serve good wines; smoking permitted.

name: Ulrich
desc: In a calm paved passage the small restaurant (Beisl) serves a breakfast and has a lunch menu.

name: LUX Restaurant
desc: One part of the establishment is a café, and the other a bar and restaurant (by the Spittelberggase entrance). The food is regional and exquisite. Free Wi-Fi.

name: Veganista
desc: Operated by two vegan sisters, this is the first vegan ice cream shop in Vienna. It has become so popular that they have now expanded with four more branches in the Vienna area. Flavours change by season, many of them ex

name: Blue Box
desc: This longstanding bar was legendary during the 1980s and 90s. It serves breakfast with many vegetarian options, as well as special beer from Vorarlberg.

name: Café Leopold
desc: A classy modern café that becomes a bar in the evening. There may be a cover charge for the evening parties downstairs.

name: Cafe Nil
desc: This Middle Eastern cafe is modeled after old coffee houses in Cairo and Alexandria, and serves many organic foods. Takeaway is available, although the atmosphere really invites one to linger.

name: Café Westend
desc: Opened in 1900, the café has historic decor with old tables and mirrors. It is situated in front of the main railway station Westbahnhof, which makes it practical to wait here for upcoming trains.

name: Das Möbel
desc: Hip café. Take a close look at the tables, chairs, and lamps – every piece of furniture is unique and for sale.

name: Espresso
desc: Very cool little 1950s-style café with good tunes, attracting an eclectic crowd. Owned by the nearby Wirr bar.

name: Europa
desc: The café is often bursting at the seams, but good tunes and decent service prevail. Good people watching and decor. One of Vienna's most popular meeting points. The bar serves warm food til late hours.

name: TartaTata
desc: This small café serves French croissants, pains au chocolat, and tartes.

name: Rote Bar
desc: Lovely interior to savour a relaxed drink inside the Volkstheater. From time to time it serves as a small venue for excellent concerts. The door is on the left side of the main entrance for the Volkstheater.

name: Siebensternbräu
desc: An excellent Biergarten. They serve their own brews, which are all excellent. There is the usual assortment of bar food, friendly staff, and outdoor seating underneath an old linden tree in the middle of a hidden courtya

name: Tunnel
desc: Student's place. Nice breakfast, live music every day starting about 21:00.

name: Puerta del Sol
desc: One of the best tapas bars in Vienna. Both the cold and warm tapas are excellent, and one can choose from amongst 90 wines.

name: Curry Insel
desc: Sri Lankan restaurant with a good range of vegetarian dishes. Free WiFi.

name: Deli Bluem
desc: The vegan restaurant cooks local ingredients.

name: Il Sestante
desc: This Italian restaurant serves pizza fired in a stone oven. It has a nice view of the Maria Treu plaza, with outdoor seating in the summer.

name: Konoba
desc: The delicious aromas of garlic and grilled fish invite the passerby into this Croatian seafood restaurant.

name: Prinz Ferdinand
desc: An Austrian Beisl that serves good food and even some vegetarian options.

name: Schnattl
desc: For more than 25 years the restaurant has been serving Viennese and international cuisine of a high standard.

name: Speisekammer
desc: A small new fancy underground restaurant, with a rotating roster of young chefs who prepare freely-improvised dishes. A special feature is the surprise menu (Überraschungsmenu), where you can choose the ingredients of yo

name: Cafe der Provinz
desc: Cute little coffee place sells mostly organic products. Serves breakfast, gallettes, and crêpes.

name: Café Eiles
desc: This café has been operating since 1840, when the building was completed. The interior dates from the last redesign in 1933.

name: Café Florianihof
desc: A very popular café that has been redecorated. It serves good food with many vegetarian options for fair prices and typical Austrian desserts like "Topfen-knöderl" or "Powiderl-Tascherl". Free Wi-Fi. Most of the places a

name: Café Merkur
desc: On Saturdays and Sundays offers breakfast almost all day. Due to its good prices it is a popular hang-out for students. Has Wi-Fi access.

name: Kaffeemodul
desc: A tiny coffee gem in Vienna, easily overlooked by passersby, with very skilled baristas.

name: People on Caffeine
desc: Hidden away in a former Catholic sacristy, this café offers fair trade and special roasted coffee. Serves espresso and many of the newer filtered coffee styles.

name: Gürtel
desc: Many bars and music-oriented venues are under the elevated subway tracks.

name: B72
desc: The bar also serves as a venue for hip hop and modern music concerts.

name: Chelsea
desc: Serving a wide range of international beers, this popular place is often fully-packed.

name: Rhiz
desc: Rhiz promotes experimental music for an alternative audience; it's well worth checking out the online program of upcoming concerts. This bar tends to be particularly smoky.

name: Café Do An
desc: Several salads are served. Free Wi-Fi. Usually it is well packed by a "bobo" public.

name: Eis-Greissler
desc: Serves vegan and interesting ice-cream varieties.

name: Natsu I
desc: Decent sushi.

name: Cafe Willendorf
desc: The restaurant inside the lesbian and queer "Rosa Lilla Villa" serves good international food.

name: Disco Volante
desc: Pizza with just enough and not too many toppings, and very Italian selection. Austrian ingredients, when used, are unusual specialties.

name: Kuishimbo
desc: The smallest Japanese restaurant in town. All the dishes are homemade, and the owners claim that they pay attention to a proper balance of ingredients – being full can also be healthy. The place is so small that there is

name: Mythos
desc: A nice family-run Greek restaurant, with a good variety of items to choose from.

name: Naschmarkt Deli
desc: Popular student meet place in Naschmarkt that sells directly sells good food with many vegetarian options directly from the Naschmarkt. The Italian café is recommended. Later in the evenings often a DJ plays.

name: Salzberg
desc: The Salzberg restaurant serves Pongauer Kasnocken, made with special smoked cheese (Räucherkäse) from Salzburg province. There is a large selection of breakfast/brunch choices. The open air patio is on a quiet street.

name: Schwarze Katze
desc: Georges Dimou, the singer, operates this traditional Greek restaurant.

name: Fischrestaurant Umar
desc: Extremely good fish directly from their shop, which is the best and freshest seafood shop in Vienna. Wi-Fi is available. Changing daily lunch menu.

name: Neni
desc: The best restaurant on the Naschmarkt with Isrealean carte.

name: Café Drechsler
desc: The café is open during nights. It opened in 1919 by Engelbert Drechsler and is a traditional and popular all-night meeting point. It was carefully remodeled in 2007.

name: Cafe Jelinek
desc: Small coffee place nicely lost in the middle of Mariahilf. In winter the rustic and warm oven is wonderful. In summer one can sit outdoors.

name: Cafe Restaurant Gschamster Diener
desc: Smaller congenial Viennese café.

name: Café Ritter
desc: A traditional Viennese cafe that is very popular due to its central location on Mariahilfer Strasse.

name: Café Savoy
desc: The queer bar is centered around a big mirror and decorated in Makart style (Makartstil). Free WiFi. The café serves breakfast.

name: Café Sperl
desc: A very traditional Viennese café, known to be frequented by contemporary Austrian writers including R. Menasse. It offers breakfast, cakes and a great atmosphere. Don't be put off by the Viennese brusqueness of the waite

name: Phil
desc: The bar/café sells also books, LPs and its furniture. The Pellini-Espresso is served from a Faema machine. Nice place to have breakfast.

name: Topkino
desc: The bar of the cinema has good food too and serves wine and beer in a relaxed atmosphere. Unfortunately only up to 22:00 the bar is non-smoking, soon before people start smoking.

name: Barfly's Club
desc: Big selection of fine and rare bottles.

name: Bar Italia
desc: The Italian styled bar offers many different cocktails. Free Wi-Fi access. The music is primarily jazz and there is a dance floor.

name: futuregarden
desc: Tiny little artsy bar, smoking permitted.

name: If dogs run free
desc: The stylish and hip bar serves interesting cocktails.

name: Joanelli
desc: The bar permits smoking and offers wines and vegan snacks.

name: Tanzcafé Jenseits
desc: The bar serves good wine, with a popular dance floor (unusual in Vienna). Well-liked by women.

name: Gasthaus Wickerl
desc: Traditional Austrian tavern from an excellent kitchen.

name: Statt-Beisl
desc: The student tavern inside of the WUK offers international food and several vegetarian offers.

name: The Highlander
desc: Offers own beer and a nice variety of dishes, including vegetarian dishes, at a small square. Might not be one of the cheapest in the cheap section, but definitely worth the price.

name: Wiener Deewan
desc: Young, urban Pakistani restaurant. All you can eat, pay as you wish. You can mix your own menu from a variety of curries, meat, rice, salads, and sauces. Vegetarians will have good choices.

name: Zuppa
desc: Nice buffet and good choice of soups including some vegan options. Take-away.

name: Lane & Merriman’s
desc: The Irish pub not only serves Irish food together with a big beer and whiskey choice it also sells bread (Blaa Bread, Treacle Bread) and apples.

name: Pizza Riva
desc: Pizza Napoletana with good flavour.

name: Rebhuhn
hours: Daily 11:00-24:00, July and August only Sa Su 18:0
desc: A classic Viennese restaurant with daily changing menu with traditional meat food plus a great choice of Knödel.

name: Stomach
desc: The restaurant serves contemporary Austrian cuisine, with many Styrian influences. It is highly rated and very popular. Reservations are recommended.

name: Zum roten Bären
desc: The restaurant serves Austrian food classics combined with Slovenian food with great quality cooked by Hans Bodingbauer. It has Černá-Hora beer and interesting white wines per glass sold cheaply.

name: Flein
desc: On the French ground of the French culture institute this restaurant serves good food. The lunch menu consists of two choices with one being vegetarian. Dogs are not allowed. In the nice season one can enjoy the garden.

name: Good Morning Vietnam
desc: Vietnamese authentic restaurant serving refined food.

name: Charlie P's Pub and Dining Room
desc: The Irish pub is very popular. It sells of course Irish beer, and fish and chips. It has a wide non-smoking area.

name: Halbestadt
desc: The cocktail bar fills quickly, hence it is considered wise to reserve places. The cocktails are done with lots of knowledge and excellent alcohols. Consider asking for their specials as they give good advice. The barkee

name: Stiegl Ambulanz
desc: A good bar run by the Stiegl brewery where you can enjoy their beer, which is one of Austria's best common beers. The bar is popular for students with its modern furnishings and relaxed atmosphere. Try the Paracelsus, wh

name: The Sign
desc: This lounge bar serves experimental cocktails by trained keepers. The cocktails are very laboriously mixed. Very friendly service. From the outside the bar is almost not noticeable, but elongates towards the interior. Th

name: Weinstadt
desc: Every Wednesday the wine bar organises a specific wine tasting. One can choose between many Austrian or international wines.

name: Universitats Brauhaus
desc: Charming beer garden in the Altes AKH campus of the University of Vienna. They serve traditional Viennese pub food as well as excellent BBQ ribs.

name: Café Stein
desc: A café that is a popular students' meeting point. It has modern stylish interior.

name: Café Francais
desc: The brasserie offers a simple French bistro food choice.

name: Café Weimar
desc: A traditional Viennese café where one can listen every day after 19:30 to piano music.

name: Weltcafé
desc: The café serves fairtrade food and café. Free Wi-Fi.

name: Vegetasia
desc: Chain of vegetarian restaurants. Serves a huge variety of Taiwanese Buddhist vegetarian food. Most of it vegan, many meat imitations. Non-smoking.

name: Rochusmarkt
desc: Typical Viennese outdoor market with fresh produce as well as stalls selling baked goods and other prepared food.

name: Amon
desc: The restaurant serves seasonal Viennese food typically of course plates with large quantities. The cellar is a vinothek with a good selection of Austrian wines.

name: Benkei
desc: Favorite place from nearby Japanese embassy. The place has a bit dated interior.

name: El Fontroussi
desc: The Belgium restaurant in this renovated tavern offers seafood with refined sauces. Daily lunch menu.

name: Marx Restauration
desc: The restaurant inside an old butchery serves modern Viennese food. Free Wi-Fi.

name: No. 27
desc: The Chinese restaurant is best visited with several persons to be able to taste their different plates.

name: O'Connor's Old Oak
desc: Gareth "Gaz" Smith is cooking here daily, hence this Irish pub may serve the best Irish food in Vienna (not only legendary fish and chips).

name: Pho & Saigon Market NR
desc: A Vietnamese restaurant next to the shop has small delicate choices. The cellar has one table tennis.

name: Sri Thai Imbiss
desc: The small cellar place cooks Thai food (green curry,..) on the spicy side of life.

name: Taverna Lefteris
desc: The Cretan (not Greek) restaurant changes its menu daily.

name: Rochus
desc: Contemporary Viennese and European cuisine. Vegan options available. Extensive wine and cocktail list.

name: al Italiana
desc: Traditional Italian pizzeria and trattoria. Friendly service, extensive menu, good wine list. Popular with locals.

name: Meierei im Stadtpark
desc: The very posh restaurant offers 120 different cheese varieties combined with freshly baked Viennese bread. This is the "bistro" of the Steiereck, but still extremely classy.

name: Steirereck im Stadtpark
desc: The most renowned Austrian restaurant in middle of the beautiful Stadtpark is defintely worth a visit. Heinz Reitbauer is cooking with exotic or mostly forgotten natural herbs. Much of the menu features modernistic prese

name: That’s Amore
desc: Italian cooks use well chosen products for their pizzas.

name: Cafe Menta
desc: Designed by Robin Molenaar and Yvonne Krisch with Rainer seats and an industrial bar, the café has a cool look plus interesting vegetarian options.

name: Intermezzo Bar
desc: Incredible lustre above the bar from the 1960s.

name: Salm Bräu
desc: The brewery has a Viennese kitchen, but people mostly come for the good beer.

name: Strandbar Hermann
desc: The outdoor bar serves daily happy hour cocktails during 18:00-19:00. As the name tells it is a bar on sand next to the Danube canal near the Urania.

name: Pizza Mari
desc: A very authentic and chic napolitanian pizza parlor. Large, delicious pizzas and a range of Italian food. The wine card has interesting Austrian white wine choices.

name: Harvest
desc: Vegan and vegetarian café serving good food. One can choose between interesting regional and international beers and wines.

name: Lusthaus
hours: Oct-Apr: Th-Tu 12:00-18:00; May-Sep: M Tu Th F 12:
desc: Built in 1784 as a lodge for imperial hunting parties, the unusual octagonal building has served as a restaurant since the end of the monarchy. Serves traditional Austrian fare.

name: Möslinger
desc: This tavern serves food from the nearby Waldviertel region; specialties include carp, poppy seed cake, and beer.

name: Pancho
desc: Decent Austro-Mex food, but come for the cocktails.

name: Schöne Perle
desc: Contemporary Austrian and international food. Stylish yet informal restaurant with good lunch specials. English menu. Separate non-smoking section; takeout available.

name: Restaurant Mraz Sohn
desc: Serves classic Viennese cuisine.

name: Skopik & Lohn
desc: A very low-key, classy yuppie restaurant.

name: Schweizerhaus
desc: Large beer garden, some say they have the best beer in Vienna and they also offer traditional Austrian dishes at moderate prices. Also well-known for its excellent Stelze (knuckle of pork).

name: Prater Dome
desc: Austria's largest club. Come dressed like euro-trash to get in. Thursday is ladies' night with free entry and drinks. Popular with the young conservative working class.

name: Bricks
desc: A small bar with a DJ and dance floor. It is a very local place and the crowd is an array of people of all ages from the neighborhood.

name: Fluc und Fluc Wanne
desc: An upstairs bar and its downstairs club-like half Fluc Wanne (meaning tub). Most of the club is underground in a former underpass, so do not miss it. More alternative with very diverse DJs and bands.

name: Pratersauna

name: Schank zum Reichsapfel
desc: This Vienna Heurigen serves both excellent wines, native juices, Murauer beer and cold specialities from the Schneeberg or Carinthian Gailtal.

name: Left Bank of the Donaukanal
desc: During the warm season, the riverbank gets incredibly lively in the evenings. Find a wide range of bars with artificial beaches serving cocktails, among them the very trendy [http://www.adriawien.at Adria] or [http://nen

name: On
desc: A Chinese/Asian restaurant that gets consistent excellent gourmet reviews.

name: Rudi's Beisl
desc: This Austrian Beisl likes to put "Panier" on everything.

name: Silberwirt
desc: The "Beisl" is very popular amongst local Viennese.

name: Waldviertler Hof
desc: This traditional Vienna restaurant offers good seasonal food and beer choices. The restaurant is non-smoking. Each room is specifically decorated, one of them is a traditional Zirben-Stube. The prices are fair and the po

name: Weinschenke Franzensgasse
desc: Chef Nikolai Kölbl serves enchanting versions of Viennese food. There are vegetarian options and the salads are good.

name: Woracziczky
desc: A modern interpretation of traditional Viennese food like Tafelspitzsulz, Blunzentascherln, Zwiebelrostbraten, and Kalbsrahmgulasch. It is particularly popular for its casual atmosphere and tasty, delicate food.

name: Zum Schwarzen Adler
desc: The "Gasthaus" serves Viennese food and Hackl Bräu (workers' beer).

name: propeller
desc: Cozy breakfast/lunch cafe with popular cocktails at night

name: Senhor Vinho
desc: The Portuguese restaurant offers Bacalhao, Pastel de Nata and many different Portuguese wines.

name: Café Cuadro
desc: The café serves breakfast, later cocktails and burgers, beware that people are heavily smoking.

name: Café Rüdigerhof
desc: The Rüdigerhof is a typical Viennese café, hence expect rude waiters (treat them with humor) and have enough time to chill out. It offers nice seats outdoor under trees next to the Vienna river. Indoor can be very smoky.

name: Motto
desc: It is a bar, a restaurant, a gallery and a concert location. The bar serves good wines and cocktails. It is a location for smokers.

name: Pub Klemo
desc: The wine bar and shop has an incredible choice over 3000 different wines.

name: Reinprechtsstüberl
desc: It serves upper Austrian monastery beer Schlägl and must ("Most").

name: Transporter Bar
desc: The popular minimalistic bar with fair trade juices, long drinks features life DJ acts. It has free Wi-Fi access. The table-tennis table is used every Wednesday for a ping-pong evening.

name: WerkzeugH
desc: The young architect Manfred Wuits together with the cook Zeljko Jovanovic transformed the previous tool hall/shop to an innovative popular bohemian bar. In summer time one can sit outside. There is free Wi-Fi. Usually on

name: Vorstadtwirt
desc: Classic Viennese cuisine in a typical old-style neighbourhood pub with old and well preserved wooden walls. Small regular menu but vast, often changing, seasonal selection of dishes.

name: Donauturm Café
desc: On a sunny day you can have a look over Vienna from the rotating restaurant. It is a non-smokers' restaurant.

name: Sunken City
desc: A cluster of bars, clubs and restaurants on the Donauinsel, especially popular among the younger crowds on summer evenings.

name: Purple Eat
desc: The social project integrates people without official working permits. The menu changes daily and is based on local organic food.

name: Tichy
desc: A famous Viennese place for ice cream. Famous for its Eismarillenknödel (small dumplings of vanilla ice cream with an apricot core) and Himbeereisknödel (raspberry core, vanilla ice cream, coating of ground poppy seeds).

name: Gasthaus Stafler
desc: The tavern serves specialities from southern Tirol including Trentiner Salsicce, Südtiroler Roggenteig-Schlutzkrapfen and Graukäse.

name: Der Ringsmuth
desc: Der Ringsmuth serves traditional Austrian cuisine (including tasty Wiener Schnitzel of both pork and veal) among other dishes. Spacious, with pleasant minimalistic decor. Easily accessible as it's pretty much right next

name: Kent Restaurant
desc: At first approach, this looks like a greasy kebab joint strictly for Turks, but struggle past the first room and you will find a large garden and huge restaurant serving moderately priced food with an infinite supply of

name: Pizzeria Mafiosi
price: Pizzas start at €3.20 and you can get a

name: Hollerei
desc: Vegetarian restaurant with a small but cozy outdoor dining space.

name: Salettl!Salletl!
desc: The restaurant next to the Bodenkultur university sees many students visitors. It has a great view plus romantic garden. It is a smokers place.

name: Schutzhaus am Heuberg
desc: The restaurant serves Austrian and Indian food. This unusual combination is an integration project.

name: Schutzhaus Waidäcker
desc: The place has a very rustic charm and serves rural specialities from around Austria. Vegetarian choices are limited.

name: Wetter
desc: The cook Raetus Wetter serves wonderful Italian food with daily adapted choices.

name: Klee am Hanslteich
desc: Monika Wlaschek opened this outdoor lounge with view on a small pond. It is on the Stadtwanderweg 3.

name: Pfarrwirt
desc: This highly-acclaimed establishment is operated by the winery Mayer am Pfarrplatz (see listing below). Part of the restaurant is housed in a 12th-century building known as the 'Beethoven House', as it was the composer's

name: Schrammelbeisl
desc: Christoph Stepan is cooking food at this revived tavern from the nearby Waldviertel region (meat from Litschau).

name: Wirtshaus Steirerstöckl
hours: W-Su and holidays 11:30-24:00; kitchen open until
desc: Built as a hiking lodge, this rustic Gasthaus is in the Wienerwald on the outskirts of the city. It serves classic Styrian food and wine, and also offers a few modern dishes for vegetarians. During nice weather meals can

name: 10er Marie
desc: The Heuriger, dating back to 1740, serves typical Viennese food.

name: Heuriger Hirt
desc: The Heuriger Hirt has a great view over the Danube and is hidden in the middle of vineyards in a steep section of the Leopoldsberg hill.

name: Heuriger Sissi Huber
desc: The Heuriger has a great view over Vienna. It serves also vegetarian sides.

name: Mayer am Pfarrplatz
desc: A traditional winery since 1683, operating a popular Heuriger (wine garden) and highly-acclaimed restaurant (see listing above).

name: Cafe C. I.
desc: The place on the Yppenmarkt has specific vegetarian foods and attracts a mixed public. The café has existed since 1895.

name: Kurkonditorei Oberlaa
desc: This stylish café offers breakfast and lunch too, but it is famous for its delicious cakes and pastries. It is non-smoking.

name: Fischer Bräu
desc: The brewery brews according the "Reinheitsgebot from 1516" and offers their beers. The place is very well visited.

name: Schlumberger Kellerwelten
desc: The tour in the cellar of one of the biggest Austrian "Sekt" producers takes approximately an hour, and there are up to 5 different glasses for tasting included.

name: Shiraz

name: Travel Shack Vienna
desc: A largely young student and international backpacker bar where it's hard not to meet people.

name: Gasthaus Lindwurm
desc: The place has retro charm. There is a nearby playground for kids, hence it is a very family-friendly Austrian restaurant. The place directly borders the Viennese woods.

name: Kichererbse
desc: The shop has a changing daily lunch vegan plate, salads and soup.

name: Napoleonwald
desc: The restaurant specialises in fresh fish. It is also very kid-friendly.

name: Hermes Café Restaurant Labstelle
desc: The restaurant is non-smoking and serves breakfast till 11:30.

name: Café Dommayer
desc: Nonsmoking, without outdoor seating.

name: Cafe Gloriette
desc: Inside the Gloriette with good view over to the Schönbrunn palace serves early breakfast, café and cakes. One has to climb up the hill of the Schönbrunn park to reach it.

name: Café am Platz
desc: It serves all day breakfast

name: Landtmann’s Jausen Station
desc: The renovated Meierei serves good breakfast between 09:00-14:00 in this beautiful location.

name: Heurigenschenke Zur Wildsau
desc: The Heurigen has a big garden with a good view over Vienna.

name: Schneider-Gössl
desc: The oldest Heurigen in the Ober St. Veit part of Hietzing.

name: Zum Markgraf
desc: The restaurant offers modern food with lots of vegetarian choices in a relaxed modern ambiente. It serves a good selection of local juices and wines.

name: Eulenspiegel das Bierlokal
hours: Tu-Th 18:00-23:00, F Sa 18:00-24:00, Su and holida

name: Inföhr Sekt
desc: One of the largest producers of Austrian pearled wine.

name: Mautwirtshaus

name: Babenbergerhof
desc: An excellent restaurant which serves classic Austrian dishes, operating in the Babenbergerhof Hotel (see listing below under 'Sleep').
